top_cited_works.title: Ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy of graphene oxides
top_cited_works.abstract: Dispersions of few-layer (1-3 layers), multi-layer (4-10 layers) and thick-layer (>10 layers) graphene oxide (GO) were prepared by a modified Hummers method with different mass ratios of KMnO4 to graphite. Ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) spectroscopic data show that few-layer GO dispersions can be distinguished from multi- and thick-layer dispersions by a more intense peak at 230 nm. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) images of few-layer GO contain a single peak, those of multi-layer GO exhibit a shoulder and those of thick-layer GO do not contain a peak or shoulder. These findings allow qualitative analysis of GO dispersions. X-ray photoelectron spectra (XPS) show that the change of UV-vis absorption intensity of GO is caused by a conjugative effect related to chromophore aggregation that influences the π-π* plasmon peak.

Microwave‐Assisted Preparation of White Fluorescent Graphene Quantum Dots as a Novel Phosphor for Enhanced White‐Light‐Emitting Diodes
top_cited_works.abstract: Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) with white fluorescence are synthesized by a microwave‐assisted hydrothermal method using graphite as the precursor. A solution‐processed white‐light‐emitting diode (WLED) is fabricated using the as‐prepared white fluorescent GQDs (white‐light‐emitting graphene quantum dots, WGQDs) doped 4,4‐bis(carbazol‐9‐yl)biphenyl as the emissive layer. White‐light emission is obtained from the WLED with 10 wt% doping concentration of WGQDs, which shows a luminance of 200 cd m−2 at the applied voltage of 11–14 V. Importantly, an external quantum efficiency of 0.2% is achieved, which is the highest among all the reported WLED based on GQDs or carbon dots. The results demonstrate that WGQDs as a novel phosphor may open up a new avenue to develop the environmentally friendly WLEDs for practical application in solid‐state lighting.

Co-tuning ultrathin ZnO films and programmable 3D textures to control lunar dust simulant adhesion
recent_works.abstract: Lunar regolith dust is angular, polydisperse, and electrostatically active, adhering to surfaces, obscuring optics, and accelerating wear. Using the compositionally relevant lunar dust simulant (LDS) LHS-1, we evaluate a co-tunable surface platform that integrates two-photon lithography (TPL)–printed hierarchical textures with atomic-layer-deposited (ALD) ZnO coatings (0–8 nm). The textures combine lotus-like lobes and sandfish-inspired ridges with controlled rotational registries (0°, 2.5°, 30°) as a single geometric variable. LDS retention was quantified using a standardized 20 s vibration protocol in ambient air. Once ZnO thickness reached ≥ 2 nm, surface dust coverage fell below 1%, outperforming all space-heritage materials (glass, polytetrafluoroethylene, Ti, stainless steel). Sub-continuous coatings (0.5–2 nm) already reduced adhesion of large aggregates, and atomic-force-microscopy confirmed an island-to-film transition coinciding with this threshold. With ZnO chemistry held constant, texture geometry governed the locations of retained particles, producing edge-pinning, valley capture, and ridge-bridge modes. recent_works.title: Research progress on comprehensive utilization technology of titanium-bearing blast furnace slag: a review
recent_works.abstract: Titanium-bearing blast furnace slag (Ti-bearing BF slag) is a major industrial by-product generated during the blast furnace smelting of vanadium–titanium iron concentrate. More than 50% of the titanium resources in vanadium–titanium magnetite are transferred into the slag phase during smelting, making Ti-bearing BF slag an important secondary titanium resource. However, titanium components in Ti-bearing BF slag are highly dispersed in multiple Ti-rich mineral phases, such as perovskite, titanaugite, titanium-rich diopside, titanium carbonitride, and magnesium–aluminum spinel. These phases generally have fine particle sizes, commonly less than 10 μm, and similar surface physicochemical properties, making efficient separation by conventional beneficiation methods extremely difficult. Consequently, large quantities of Ti-bearing BF slag have long been stockpiled, resulting in serious titanium resource loss and substantial land occupation. In this review, current technologies for the comprehensive utilization of Ti-bearing BF slag are systematically summarized and classified into non-titanium-extraction and titanium-extraction routes.
